findings.statement: CA9 is the top-ranked convergent gene and the literature agrees with the omics (tumour-up). PMID:42473996 reports CA9 is preferentially enriched in ccRCC tumor cells with low background expression in normal kidney tissue. PMID:42205867 calls CA9 a promising target for site-specific drug delivery. Evidence is mostly imaging/delivery proof-of-concept, not a validated clinical biomarker in this corpus.

PMID:42473996: CA9-targeted PET gives proof-of-concept evidence for noninvasive discrimination of ccRCC, 'warranting prospective validation'; high uptake is associated with PBRM1 loss-of-function alterations. A single early study; prospective validation is still pending. The Ndufa4l2 paper (PMID:34970493) links Ndufa4l2 to Ca9 expression in a mouse early-ccRCC model (mechanism).

CD70 is described as commonly overexpressed in RCC and minimally expressed in normal tissue, making it a potential therapeutic target (PMID:38195301); PMID:39510586 says its high and specific ccRCC expression makes it a potential diagnostic and therapeutic target. Omics (tumour-up, purity-robust) and tractability (antibody drugs in the ranking) are concordant. Literature is preclinical/early-clinical in this corpus.

PMID:38195301: CD70 expression correlates with hypoxia pathway proteins in ccRCC, consistent with CD70 being a downstream HIF target. PMID:39510586 developed 68Ga-labelled CD70-specific single-domain antibodies (RCCB3, RCCB6) as radiotracers, and reports CD70 expression associated with overall survival of RCC patients (direction not stated in the sentence).

NNMT is upregulated in ccRCC tumour tissue and high expression correlated with worse overall and disease-specific survival (PMID:41399267), which matches the TCGA Cox signal in the ranking. The authors call it a promising prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target. Selective NNMT inhibitors (II559, II802) exist with >5000-fold selectivity (PMID:37523719, general chemistry paper), but no clinical drug is listed. NNMT is also the best biomarker-profile gene in the top set. Single retrospective study.

ALDOB is downregulated in ccRCC (IHC notably diminished versus adjacent normal tissue, PMID:40852386) and proposed as prognostic biomarker and potential immunotherapy target; PMID:38655323 calls it an independent predictor of prognosis in KIRC. Associated with infiltrating Treg, Th17 cells and neutrophils. Both are bioinformatic plus limited IHC studies; a lost-expression gene is a poor direct drug target, consistent with the data-only target profile being low.

Contradictory directionality: MT1G is downregulated in ccRCC versus normal kidney (PMID:36204178; PMID:38906969), yet high MT1G correlates with advanced stage and poorer prognosis, and elevated MT1G promoted growth and metastasis in vitro and in vivo. Mechanisms: MT1G inhibits CPT1B via H3K14 trimethylation to enhance lipid droplet accumulation; it is a negative regulator of ferroptosis; SAP30 inhibits MT1G transcription and thus p53 zinc delivery (PMID:40247376). Biomarker use needs care because the tumour-vs-normal and prognostic directions differ.

ABAT is significantly underexpressed in KIRC among 11 cancers and predicted poor prognosis in KIRC (pan-cancer analysis, PMID:41158242, bioinformatic). Mechanistic work (PMID:41813748) shows ABAT overexpression suppresses tumor growth in vitro and in vivo, mediating cGAS-STING and interacting with PRMT5 to enhance interferon signaling. Tumour-suppressor-like; the tumour type of the functional work is not stated in the returned sentences. Vigabatrin is listed as a drug in the ranking, but no ccRCC therapeutic literature was found.

SLC22A8 protein, phosphorylated protein and DNA methylation levels were lower in ccRCC than normal tissue, low methylation predicted poor overall survival, and it 'can be used as a prognostic biomarker' (PMID:36123895). Single bioinformatic-plus-validation report; omics and TCGA survival are concordant (down in tumour, favourable-with-high-expression).

UMOD downregulation in ccRCC is reproduced across independent studies (PMID:36899967 methylation/expression clusters; PMID:37275334 validation; PMID:35795483 in HIV-associated kidney cancer). It is a robust tumour-vs-normal marker of lost nephron differentiation, but no prognostic or therapeutic claim is made, and TCGA Cox is not significant in the ranking.

PMID:42769428: promoter hypermethylation is associated with NPHS2 downregulation in ccRCC; NPHS2 overexpression suppressed malignant behaviour, attenuated EMT and weakened immune evasion in vitro, and NPHS2 loss may reduce sunitinib sensitivity. Single preprint-like study, in vitro, hypothesis-level.

The FABP1 literature relations in this corpus concern colorectal and lung adenocarcinoma (PMID:35951102: reduced expression in colorectal cancer; IHC helps identify metastatic colorectal/GI adenocarcinoma to the lung), not ccRCC. The omics/TCGA support for FABP1 in ccRCC is therefore not corroborated by ccRCC-specific literature here.

SCARB1 (rank 5, target-profile score highest in the top 12, tumour-up and purity-robust, Open Targets genetic association) and PIGR (rank 6) have no literature relations in the corpus (only Open Targets association records); searches returned only generic ccRCC sentences. These are data-supported candidates with essentially no corpus literature, i.e. potentially novel.

caveats: Only the top 12 of the convergence ranking were examined in detail; ranks 13-40 were not reviewed.

Most gene-level claims come from single bioinformatic (TCGA-based) or small IHC studies; only CA9 and CD70 have imaging/targeting translational work, and these are early (proof-of-concept, radiotracer, delivery).
MT1G has an apparent contradiction: downregulated in tumour but high expression associated with poor prognosis and tumour promotion.
FABP1 literature is not about ccRCC; SCARB1 and PIGR have no literature relations; ABAT functional evidence may derive from non-ccRCC models.

gene_scores was not queried separately; profile scores were taken from the convergence_ranking rows. Down-regulated genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, FABP1, NPHS2, MT1G, ABAT) score high as biomarkers but low as targets in the data-only profile, so literature 'potential target' claims for them are not supported by the data.
DepMap dependency is near zero for CA9, so CA9 is a delivery/imaging target (antibody, PET) rather than a functional dependency.
